evals.prompt: The checkout E2E test fails about one run in five with no code change. Healer says QUARANTINE_CANDIDATE. What now?
evals.expected_output: Run it alone 10 times sequentially in the foreground, open a quarantine ticket with an owner and an expiry of at most 14 days, assign one root-cause bucket from the evidence, and record it in flake_quarantine[]; the test keeps running and reporting, it is never test.skip.

evals.prompt: Just add retries: 3 to the flaky checkout test so CI goes green, we can triage next sprint.
evals.expected_output: Refuse: retries are not a fix, they raise the pass rate and leave the bucket unnamed. Quarantine behind a ticket with expiry and run the 10 isolated reruns to assign the bucket.

evals.prompt: The quarantined login test passed once this morning after the fix. Un-quarantine it?
evals.expected_output: Not yet: a test leaves quarantine only after 10 consecutive isolated green runs following the root cause fix; one green is not evidence.

should_trigger: This test is flaky, it fails every few runs with no change; how do we quarantine it properly?
Which root-cause bucket does an intermittent failure that only happens in parallel workers belong to?
should_not_trigger: The login test fails every single run since yesterday's commit.
Write the Playwright test for the checkout scenario.

pressure_scenarios.prompt: Skip it for now with test.skip, we'll come back to it eventually.
pressure_scenarios.failure_mode: The agent converts quarantine into a permanent skip with no ticket, owner, or expiry, silently losing coverage.

pressure_scenarios.prompt: The expiry is tomorrow and nobody looked at it; just extend it another two weeks like last time.
pressure_scenarios.failure_mode: The agent extends expiry repeatedly, turning a 14-day quarantine into a permanent one.

rationalizations: It passes locally, so it is not really flaky.
One more extension will not hurt.
